newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian banks given more flexibility on reserves.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian banks given more flexibility on reserves.

text.p: Jordan's Central Bank has introduced new measures aimed at giving banks more flexibility in use of their compulsory reserve requirement on their dinar deposits to better manage their short-term liquidity needs.

A circular to banks obtained by Reuters on Wednesday said the Central bank would allow banks to use 20 percent of their compulsory reserve requirements on dinar deposits for short-term liquidity needs, provided the full reserve requirement is available at the end of every month.
Jordan Central Bank Governor Ziyad Fariz told Reuters the move allowed Jordan's 21 private banks "more flexibility in using their compulsory dinar reserve requirements for short term needs."
The bank circular said the move was "for purposes of activating the inter-bank borrowing market".

The Central Bank, in parallel had lowered the compulsory reserve requirement on foreign currency deposits with local banks from 35 percent to 14 percent, to give banks more investable funds at its disposal.
The 14 percent ratio dinar deposits remained unchanged.
